messages:
claire-support: raising ticket #1452 — multiple customers reporting p95 spike for text-generation endpoint after today's runtime v2.9 rollout. p95 up ~2.8x, p99 worse. sample trace: https://traces.redwood/abc :eyes:
eng-runtime-oncall: looking. which customers / models?
claire-support: two orgs, both on gpt-open-3b, sequences ~512-2048. spike lines up with 11:28 global rollout. ticket includes perf graphs.
sam: saw canary blip at 11:20, traffic ramped to 100% around 11:28. I kept an eye but initial signals were green.
maria: note recent kernel-selector tweak — it favors fused kernels when avg_seq < 256. that could regress long-seq paths if traffic mix shifts.
josh: confirm. new selector flag `prefer_fused_attn=true` shipped in v2.9. can cause kernel thrash when mixed seqs land on same pool.
eng-runtime-oncall: can we revert traffic policy to previous split while we triage? cc @sam
sam: rolling traffic-policy back to previous 80/20 at 11:55, will monitor.
deploy-bot: traffic-policy rollback initiated by @sam at 1719999955
claire-support: after rollback customers still see elevated p95 at 12:02, p95 down a bit but p99 remains high.
maria: also check `batcher.max_batch_size` — that was raised from 8->32 in this rollout for throughput gains. mixed long/short sequences can cause queueing.
josh: testing a quick patch: set `batcher.max_batch_size=8` for pool-42 and disable `continuous_batching` on heavy-seq routes.
eng-runtime-oncall: applying config to pool-42 now.
claire-support: repro steps from support: run long-seq request to /models/generate with seq=1024 and check tail latency. customers provided curl:
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood/models/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-3b","input":"aaaaaaaa... (1024 chars)","max_tokens":8}'
```
maria: baseline before rollout: p95 ~220ms for that repro. after rollout: p95 ~610ms, p99 ~1.2s. logs show queuing spikes and repeated kernel fallbacks.
josh: traces show high `kernel_swap` events around step 1; CPU waits and small kernels thrashing.
sam: temporary mitigation options: 1) pin affected customers to runtime v2.8, 2) route them to dedicated pool with conservative config, 3) lower batcher.max_batch_size globally for pool. which do we want?
claire-support: customers prefer dedicated routing short-term over being pinned — less disruptive.
maria: I recommend: revert kernel-selector change in canary, keep `max_batch_size=8` for mixed pools, run new canary on traffic with long-seq profiles.
josh: agree. I'll prepare kernel-selector rollback diff and a config patch. also add metric `kernel_swap_rate` alerts.
eng-runtime-oncall: created bug INF-3145 for rollback + config changes. owner @maria. target hotfix by EOD, canary tomorrow 09:00.
claire-support: updated support ticket and notified customers about temporary dedicated routing. they acknowledged. :thumbsup:
sam: monitoring metrics — p95 back down ~35% from peak after pool config tweak. continuing to watch next 30m.
claire-support: thanks team. will reopen if new reports come in.
